standard_prerequisites.name: Existence of a monic polynomial modulo the ideal vanishing at a lift of the idempotent
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the polynomial f whose factorisation drives the construction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Factorisation of that polynomial after an etale base change inducing an isomorphism modulo the ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the two factors g and h congruent to a variable power and to a power of the variable minus one modulo the ideal.

standard_prerequisites.name: An integral ring map is closed on spectra, and closed disjoint loci can be separated by an element
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemmas \ref{algebra-lemma-integral-going-up} and \ref{algebra-lemma-going-up-closed}, cited at proof lines 2007-2009, and Lemma \ref{lemma-separate-image-closed-from-closed}, cited at proof lines 2010-2012
standard_prerequisites.use: Produce the element whose localisation makes the two loci cover the spectrum.

standard_prerequisites.name: Idempotents correspond to open and closed subsets, and the associated idempotent is unique
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-disjoint-decomposition}, cited at proof lines 2014 and 2017
standard_prerequisites.use: Give the idempotent of the disjoint decomposition and identify it as the required lift.

core_obligations: Choose a lift of the idempotent and an integrality polynomial for it (proof lines 1988-1989).
Make the etale base change and factor the polynomial into the two prescribed factors (proof lines 1990-1994).
Evaluate the factors at the lift to obtain two elements multiplying to zero that lift the idempotent and its complementary part (proof lines 1995-2004).
Separate the two vanishing loci from the locus of the ideal using closedness and the separation lemma, and localise at the separating element (proof lines 2005-2013).
Conclude that the two loci are disjoint and cover the spectrum, and take the resulting idempotent, which lifts the given one by uniqueness (proof lines 2014-2017).
proof_roadmap: Produce and factor the polynomial (proof lines 1988-1994).
Evaluate at the lift and separate the loci (proof lines 1995-2013).
Take the idempotent of the disjoint decomposition (proof lines 2014-2017).
difficulty_reason: The lemma lifts an idempotent of an integral algebra modulo an ideal after an etale base change which induces an isomorphism modulo that ideal. The proof picks a lift of the idempotent, applies the integrality helper to obtain a monic polynomial vanishing at that lift modulo the ideal, and then uses the factorisation lemma to split that polynomial, after an etale base change of the required kind, into factors congruent to a power of the variable and to a power of the variable minus one. The two evaluations of the factors at the lifted element multiply to zero, so their common vanishing locus avoids the closed set cut out by the ideal; closedness of the integral map on spectra produces a single element whose localisation separates the two loci, after which the two loci are disjoint and cover the spectrum, so that the corresponding idempotent lifts the given one by uniqueness of the splitting.
